## Problem

Lint rule GV013 (leading-wildcard-like) only looks for a pattern that starts with `%`. A pattern that starts with the single-character wildcard `_` has no literal prefix either, so a B-tree index or min/max statistics cannot narrow it down and the engine scans every value, but GV013 stays quiet:

```bash
gulliver lint "SELECT id FROM t WHERE name LIKE '%abc' LIMIT 1"
# info  GV013 leading-wildcard-like: name LIKE '%abc' starts with a wildcard ...

gulliver lint "SELECT id FROM t WHERE name LIKE '_abc' LIMIT 1"
# No scale problems found.

gulliver lint "SELECT id FROM t WHERE name ILIKE '__-123' LIMIT 1"
# No scale problems found.
```

## Where to start

- `src/gulliver/lint.py:372-381`: the GV013 check uses `pattern.name.startswith("%")`. Make it `pattern.name[:1] in ("%", "_")`.
- Keep the ESCAPE case right: `name LIKE '\_abc' ESCAPE '\'` starts with a literal underscore and must not be flagged (it already starts with `\`, so this should just work; add a test to keep it that way).
- Update the rule description in `RULES` in `src/gulliver/lint.py` (and regenerate the README lint table with `gulliver rules --format markdown`, see #18) so it mentions `_` too.
- Tests: `tests/test_lint.py:158-160` has the existing GV013 tests.

## Done when

- [ ] `LIKE '_abc'` and `ILIKE '__x%'` get GV013; `LIKE 'a_c'` and `LIKE 'x%'` do not
- [ ] the escaped case is not flagged
- [ ] the rule description and README table mention `_`
- [ ] `pytest` and `ruff check .` pass
